title: Seed OpDag Applied Set From Snapshot Merges
description: Found while verifying Wave R1c's new two-peer reconcile test (concurrent_delete_and_wire_reconciles_without_a_dangling_edge, framework/product/os/core/rs/lib.rs): DocumentVcsStore::merge_remote_snapshot (vcs/rs/lib.rs) adopts a peer's edits directly into self.envelope.vcs.edits / self.applied_edit_ids but never informs self.dag (the causal OpDag from framework/core/rs). A later real OpEnvelope whose deps reference one of those snapshot-adopted edit ids therefore fails OpDag::insert's dependency check forever (stuck Pending), since the dag's own applied/envelopes bookkeeping never learned about them. This silently drops any op sent by a peer immediately after a snapshot exchange in a two-store MemoryBackbone-paired scenario - a foundational sync correctness gap, not specific to the media graph. Fix: add a public OpDag::seed_applied(ids) that marks ids as applied without requiring their full OpEnvelope, and call it from both merge_remote_snapshot branches (the empty-envelope fast path and the incremental merge loop) with the ids just adopted.
summary: Fixed a foundational vcs sync-correctness bug found while verifying Wave R1c's new two-peer reconcile test. Two call sites adopt a peer's/persisted document's edits directly into DocumentVcsStore's applied_edit_ids without ever informing the causal OpDag: (1) DocumentVcsStore::merge_remote_snapshot (both the empty-envelope fast path and the incremental non-empty-merge loop), and (2) DocumentVcsStore::set_state (used by set_envelope, which OsStore::new calls whenever reconstructing a store from a persisted/cloned OsDocument whose applied_edit_ids is already non-empty). In both cases, a later real OpEnvelope whose declared deps reference one of those adopted edit ids would fail OpDag::insert's dependency check forever and sit stuck Pending, silently dropping the op. Root fix: added a new public OpDag::seed_applied(ids) (framework/core/rs/lib.rs, marks ids as applied without requiring their full OpEnvelope) and called it from all three adoption sites (both merge_remote_snapshot branches in vcs/rs/lib.rs, plus set_state). Verified via cargo test -p semio-framework-os -p vcs: this fix resolved the propagation half of the failing concurrent_delete_and_wire_reconciles_without_a_dangling_edge test (both peers now correctly converge on node removal + edge drop + matching conflicts). A second, separate, pre-existing bug remains in that same test (non-deterministic media-graph node-id minting during projection replay) — tracked in a new sibling ticket rather than fixed here, since it requires threading a new field through the OsOp::SpawnAppInstance shape and its call sites.
